newsitem.title: LATVIA: INTERVIEW-ASSET MANAGEMENT SEEN GROWING IN LITHUANIA.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-ASSET MANAGEMENT SEEN GROWING IN LITHUANIA.

text.p: Asset management funds are the next growth industry in Lithuania although the range of investment options will likely be limited for some time, the head of leading brokerage Vilfima, Arvydas Zabolis, said on Thursday.
Vilfima last week became the second company to acquire a license to carry out asset management activities in Lithuania.
Estonia's Hansa Investments was granted one a few weeks ago.
"Asset management activities will increase in Lithuania...a number of banks plan to acquire licenses by the autumn," Zabolis told Reuters in an interview.
"Over the next year or two, $60 million to perhaps $100 million may be invested here through asset management funds," he said.
But he added that investment instruments would remain limited for some time in Lithuania, which enjoys a stable macroeconomic climate but still needs to work on its mircroeconomic outlook.
"There are not that many investment options now...basically, you have three: equities, fixed income and bank accounts," Zabolis said.
Analysts say other investment instruments, such as pension funds, are a long way off in Lithuania.
Zabolis said Vilfima, which is the country's leading equities brokerage, would focus its attention on equities and fixed-income products.
"T-bill portfolios are popular with clients who want access to liquidity on a daily basis," he said.
He added that land investment funds could be a possibility in the future but were not a viable option at the moment because of legislative ambiguities regarding land ownership.
Dealers and analysts say asset management funds would inject much-needed liquidity into the securities market, which has been stuck in a protracted slump with falling prices and low volumes.
Asset management funds have caught on in Baltic neighbour Estonia and have helped keep its bourse liquid.
The market capitalisation of mutual funds in Estonia has risen to 1.3 billion kroons from 300 kroons over the past year.
